title: Francis (2013–2025)
hook: a Jesuit from Buenos Aires takes the name of the poor man of Assisi
carry: a poor church for the poor

segments.voice: Yesterday, a resignation: Benedict read his decision in Latin and stepped aside. Your line was he stepped down. Did you hand anything on? Today, the man elected after him. Day nine hundred thirty-three.

White smoke, a wet evening, a square full of umbrellas. A man in plain white steps onto the balcony of St Peter's and, for a moment, just stands there. Then he says good evening, like a neighbor. Before he gives the crowd his blessing, he asks them for something: to pray for him first, in silence. And he bows his head. The square, full a moment ago of noise, goes quiet. His name was Jorge Mario Bergoglio, a Jesuit and the archbishop of Buenos Aires. And the name he chose was Francis.
screen: `WHITE SMOKE, UMBRELLAS.` → `GOOD EVENING.` → `PRAY FOR ME FIRST.`

segments.voice: Start with the name. A few days later he told journalists how it happened. As the votes added up, a cardinal friend beside him hugged him and said, don't forget the poor. And the name came to him: Francis of Assisi, the man of poverty, the man of peace, who loved creation. You have met Francis of Assisi on this path before: the merchant's son who gave everything away. Second, the line. In that same talk he said how much he would like a Church that is poor, and for the poor. That became today's line. Third, the habits. He lived in a guesthouse instead of the papal apartment. On Holy Thursday he often went to a prison and washed the feet of prisoners, women and men, Catholics and others. He kept phoning ordinary people who had written to him. Small things, said deliberately. Fourth, the scripture under it all. Jesus's parable of the judgment, in the Douay-Rheims: "as long as you did it to one of these my least brethren, you did it to me." Francis pointed to that chapter of Matthew more than once. He also had critics: some Catholics found his style loose or his words unclear, and argued with his decisions on marriage and the liturgy; others felt he hadn't gone far enough. Both arguments ran through his years as pope. But the first evening already held the picture: a man who bowed before he blessed the crowd, and asked a Church to stay close to the poor.
screen: `DON'T FORGET THE POOR.` · `A CHURCH POOR, AND FOR THE POOR.` · `A GUESTHOUSE, A PRISON, A PHONE CALL.` · `THE LEAST OF THESE.` · then, large: `YOU DID IT TO ME.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: plan something simple. Settle, and breathe. Francis's style was small, deliberate acts. So think of one simple thing within reach today. Learning the name of the person who sells you coffee. Calling someone who lives alone. Giving to someone who asks, and looking them in the eye. Pick one. Don't make it bigger than it is. Picture yourself doing it, and notice where you'd be tempted to skip it. If you pray, you can ask for the nerve. If you don't, just decide. The bell holds the time.
Francis. Jorge Mario Bergoglio, a Jesuit from Buenos Aires, who took the name of Francis of Assisi because a friend told him not to forget the poor.
Your line: a poor church for the poor. Today, do the simple thing you picked, and do it in person if you can. Day nine hundred thirty-three.

howItsDone: Catholics pray for the pope by name in the Eucharistic Prayer at every Mass; parishes take up Francis's emphasis through food pantries, prison ministry and visits to the sick and lonely.

notes: Claims rule: the outline hook's 'first Jesuit and first pope from the Americas' are superlatives not in a cited text, so they are not stated.
Address to journalists: confirm the account of Cardinal Hummes ('don't forget the poor') and the line about 'a poor Church for the poor'.
Habits (Casa Santa Marta, Holy Thursday foot-washing in prisons including women and non-Catholics, phone calls): confirm wording.
Critics' summary (style, Amoris Laetitia, Traditionis Custodes; and those who felt he did too little) is general, without a cited text; Keeper to approve or soften.
The callback to Francis of Assisi assumes an earlier day on this path covered him; confirm or cut 'You met Francis of Assisi long ago on this path'.
'The picture... people often recall' is a soft claim; Keeper may cut.
Editor: cut the unsourced 'never used by a pope before' claim, 'again and again', and 'the picture people often recall'; varied the teach opener (was 'Four ways in', same as day 931).
Auditor: 'he went to prisons on Holy Thursday' implied every year; some years he went elsewhere (a care home, a refugee center), so now 'often'.
